{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success' (binary 0/1), acknowledge that while ANOVA is technically applicable, a Chi-square test of independence or logistic regression is statistically more appropriate; however, proceed with ANOVA as requested for omnibus comparison of means, noting the violation of normality assumptions.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target', 'Path Efficiency', 'Average Speed', and 'AD', conduct standard F-tests to determine if at least one paradigm mean differs from the others.",
    "Use the 'stim_summary' data view containing 76,655 rows filtered to the five specified paradigms."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check for Normality: Examine Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals of each ANOVA model. Note that 'Success' is binary and will violate normality; 'Time-to-Target' has a long right tail (max 201.39 vs mean 2.81), suggesting potential non-normality.",
    "Check for Homogeneity of Variances: Perform Levene's test or Bartlett's test across the five paradigm groups for each response variable.",
    "Check for Independence: Verify that observations (n=76,655) are independent trials; the large sample size suggests potential pseudoreplication if multiple trials per mouse are not accounted for in the error term.",
    "Check for Outliers: Inspect boxplots for extreme values, particularly in 'Time-to-Target' (max 201.39) and 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.82).",
    "Consider data transformation (e.g., log-transform for Time-to-Target) if normality is violated for continuous variables."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus F-test is significant for any continuous variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD), conduct pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD test to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "For 'Success', if ANOVA is deemed inappropriate, perform a Chi-square test of independence followed by pairwise comparisons using Fisher's Exact Test or Bonferroni-corrected proportions.",
    "Specifically test the hypothesis that 'Sham' differs from all other paradigms, given the large mean difference in 'Success' (0.27 vs ~0.68-0.78) and 'Time-to-Target' (4.68 vs ~2.5-3.1).",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared) for significant omnibus results."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Significant differences are expected for 'Success' and 'Time-to-Target', with 'Sham' performing significantly worse (lower success rate, higher time) than 'Combined', 'ICMS Only', and 'Dim Visual Only'.",
    "Significant differences are expected for 'Path Efficiency' and 'Average Speed', with 'Sham' showing lower efficiency and speed compared to stimulated groups.",
    "Significant differences are expected for 'AD' (angular dispersion), with 'Sham' showing higher dispersion (0.236) compared to other groups (0.33-0.40), indicating less precise navigation.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm may show superior performance compared to single-modality stimulation ('ICMS Only', 'Dim Visual Only', 'Bright Visual Only') based on the summary means."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption of ANOVA; a non-parametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis) or Chi-square test is preferred.",
    "The 'Time-to-Target' distribution is highly skewed (mean 2.81, max 201.39), which may inflate Type I error rates or reduce power without transformation.",
    "Potential pseudoreplication: The dataset contains 8 mouse levels with thousands of rows each; standard ANOVA treats rows as independent, ignoring the nested structure of trials within mice.",
    "Unbalanced design: Paradigm group sizes vary significantly (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846), which can affect the robustness of ANOVA assumptions."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) for each response variable with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for the nested data structure and potential non-independence of trials within the same mouse."
}
